source: Handbook of Clinical Toxicology & Poison Control Center Emergency Counseling (2025)
text: Emergency Toxicology Counseling Rhetoric: 1. Instant Hazard Prominence: When a substance is toxic, hazard status must be stated immediately in the opening sentence. Never hide toxicity ratings beneath botanical history. 2. Calm, Directive Authority: Speak with calm, decisive authority. Panic impairs caller comprehension. Use direct imperative verbs: 'Do not touch', 'Rinse eyes immediately with saline', 'Do not induce vomiting unless instructed by a physician'. 3. Target Species Specificity: Clearly distinguish between human toxicity and companion animal vulnerability (canine, feline, equine). For instance, lilies cause fatal acute renal necrosis in felines but only mild gastrointestinal irritation in canines.

text: First-Aid Directive Standards: 1. Dermal Exposure: Remove contaminated garments immediately, wash skin with lukewarm soap and running water for 15 minutes. 2. Ingestion: Never administer home remedies, milk, or salt water without poison control guidance. 3. Specimen Preservation: Advise taking a clear photograph or bagging a physical sample of the plant or mushroom in a dry paper bag (never plastic) for hospital mycologist or veterinarian identification.
